added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own arms: gate-base.log (revision 0c654ea1d, '4 failed, 147 passed') fails exactly the four new tests (test_promotion_waits_for_the_in_flight_pick_and_records_it, test_promotion_names_the_timeout_when_the_pick_never_lands, test_an_overruled_hold_records_its_own_route_mode, test_pick_outcomes_counts_an_overruled_hold_apart_from_shadow); gate-head.log (revision dd5169479, '151 passed') records no failing id, so the set difference head-minus-base is empty (0 added). Reproduced independently: the four ids fail against base product code in a git-archive scratch tree and the wait test passes at head.

findings.text: blocking: test_promotion_names_the_timeout_when_the_pick_never_lands races its own fixture — the 2.0 s pick delay can elapse during the _commit_work/_init_ledger git work that runs before crew.complete, so the deferred pick has already attached its 'route' answer and the promoted row legitimately carries action 'route', failing the expected 'fallback'. Reproduced serially in a scratch tree at ec550c27f: the 4-test file failed this id once (105 s), the id alone failed 1 of 2 isolated runs, and with delay raised to 30.0 s it passed 3 of 3 — so the reviewed head gate's '151 passed' is not reproducible and the timeout clause of the done-when rests on an unsound test. Fix by making the pick's completion the controlled event (block on an event like the sibling test) rather than racing a wall-clock delay against the intervening git work.

follow-on: _shadow_pick_deadline measures the wait window from the pointer's created_at, while the deferred pick's own bound runs from _start_shadow_picker_selection, which dispatch calls only after the worker launch (including worktree provisioning). When launch exceeds the bound, promotion can exhaust _SHADOW_PICK_WAIT_SECONDS and stamp a 'timeout' fallback while the pick is still inside its own bound; the later real answer overwrites the live pointer but not the already-committed row, so the row can report a timeout for a pick that in fact landed. The docstring says 'up to the pick's own bound'; record the pick's start stamp and measure from it.

follow-on: promoted_route_mode whitelists {picker, shadow, explicit} and returns None for the new 'overridden-hold' value, so any future row built through ledger.build_record:2528 rather than the post-hoc assignment at reckon/crew/promotion.py:1026 would silently drop it. The node records this in its manifest; extending the whitelist at reckon/ledger.py:2181 would remove the trap.
